# Intikhab Azam

> AI/ML engineer and systems architect working remotely with US teams: production voice agents, multi-tenant platforms, RAG and LLM agents, automation and open-source developer tools.

Contact: https://x.com/AzamIntikhab · Code: https://github.com/intikhab49 · Site: https://intikhab49.github.io/

## Client work (anonymized)

- Three production voice agents on the phone lines (US mobility company, Voice AI): An inbound receptionist, an outbound caller and a payment-recovery agent on Vapi. Payment links and SMS go through a Cloudflare Worker to Stripe; returning callers are recognized by caller ID. Results: Every prompt change is tested with scripted call batteries before it is pushed (30 of 30 on one branching flow); Dev and production organizations kept separate, with a promote step between them.
- A multi-tenant platform for sensitive personal data (Provider network, Multi-tenant SaaS): A NestJS and Prisma API on PostgreSQL with tenant isolation on every row, roles checked per endpoint, and a Next.js portal whose sessions stay in httpOnly cookies behind a backend-for-frontend. Results: 148 API endpoints across 26 areas, each with its roles documented; A Playwright end-to-end suite runs on every pull request; Built with a coordinated team of AI coding agents and a human developer, behind spec files and test gates.
- Slack triage for someone in 200+ channels (Agency executive, AI automation): A triage system that reads the day’s Slack and files what matters as cards on a Notion board: a keyword matrix, a Notion schema and a triage prompt checked by hand on 11 of 11 test cases. Results: Runs on a daily schedule; No new access to the client’s systems: it works through the connectors they already had.
- A company website with motion that means something (Billing-services company, Website): Designed and built the site on Cloudflare Pages with four motion systems, and built a contact form backend and a CMS for the team. Results: Live on Cloudflare Pages; Mobile spacing and overflow fixed across the whole site.
- A lead engine past the Google Places limit (Sales team, Lead generation): A self-hosted engine that grid-searches an area, falls back to OpenStreetMap, finds websites and emails, removes duplicates and resumes after a stop. Results: Built for a client’s outbound sales team; An open-source version is on GitHub.
- An AI receptionist for a dental practice (Dental practice, Voice AI): A voice receptionist on Vapi that greets callers, answers common questions and hands off to the team, set up as a working demo for the owner. Results: Tested on live phone calls before it was shown.

## Open-source projects

- [fairfax](https://github.com/intikhab49/fairfax): Is it available in GCC High? Checks a Microsoft 365 GCC, GCC High or DoD and Azure Government plan against Microsoft’s own tables, and finds commercial endpoints in code. Proof: 633 features, every row cited · weekly re-check with Wayback copies. Website: https://intikhab49.github.io/fairfax/
- [blueprint-runtime](https://github.com/intikhab49/blueprint-runtime): Test Make.com scenarios offline. Replays real Make runs locally so a broken mapping fails in CI, not in production. Proof: 71 of 79 real runs reproduced exactly, 0 differ. Website: https://intikhab49.github.io/blueprint-runtime/
- [pgvector-cpu-check](https://github.com/intikhab49/pgvector-cpu-check): Which CPU crashes your Postgres image? Runs it on 7 CPU models and names the faulting instruction behind SIGILL. Proof: 13 popular images audited · 3 build bugs found. Website: https://intikhab49.github.io/pgvector-cpu-check/
- [lifeboat](https://github.com/intikhab49/lifeboat): Bitnami’s PostgreSQL and PostgreSQL HA images, rebuilt from upstream source as drop-ins for the Bitnami Helm charts. Proof: every source SHA-256 pinned · amd64 and arm64.
- [diff-gate](https://github.com/intikhab49/diff-gate): Fails a coding agent’s diff when an import resolves to nothing, before attackers register the name. Proof: Claude Code skill and GitHub Action · zero dependencies.
- [minio-from-source](https://github.com/intikhab49/minio-from-source): A free MinIO server and mc image built from source at pinned, commit-verified releases, for amd64 and arm64. Proof: smoke-tested · on the GitHub Marketplace.
- [pushback](https://github.com/intikhab49/pushback): How often do you correct your coding agent? Measures it from Claude Code transcripts and drafts CLAUDE.md rules. Proof: on PyPI · tests in CI. PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/pushback/
- [Open Jev](https://github.com/intikhab49/open-jev-typed-decision-engine): An open 150M typed decision engine: label, choice and score in one pass, with calibrated confidence. Proof: 0.697 vs 0.727 accuracy · 2.5x better calibrated · 4x faster.
- [rag-cost-curve](https://github.com/intikhab49/rag-cost-curve): What agentic RAG really costs: cost per correct answer for four RAG designs on multi-hop questions. Proof: +32.5 exact match at 2.5x the cost per correct answer.
- [pdf-cpu-bench](https://github.com/intikhab49/pdf-cpu-bench): The best PDF-to-Markdown parser for RAG without a GPU: accuracy, seconds per page, peak RAM and install size. Proof: 9 parsers · 1,403 PDFs · MinerU CPU tier leads at 74.6%.
- [whofetched](https://github.com/intikhab49/whofetched): Which AI actually read your page? Canary links and a Cloudflare Worker log, tested on six AI apps. Proof: every log in the repo, timestamped.
- [EdgeProof](https://github.com/intikhab49/edgeproof-crypto-trading-backtest): Crypto strategy backtesting and ML validation: triple-barrier labels, purged k-fold CV, deflated Sharpe and a positive control. Proof: reports the honest result: no edge after fees.
- [vapi-voice-agent-crm](https://github.com/intikhab49/vapi-voice-agent-crm): Call ops for AI voice agents: webhook ingestion, a predictive dialer, auto-redial and Stripe-verified conversions. Proof: Vapi · Twilio · Stripe · Express.
- [local-business-lead-finder](https://github.com/intikhab49/local-business-lead-finder): Self-hosted lead generation past the Google Places 60-result cap, with an OpenStreetMap fallback and resumable runs. Proof: FastAPI · Streamlit · grid search · dedup.
- [npi-lead-pipeline](https://github.com/intikhab49/npi-healthcare-lead-pipeline): Provider directory to practice websites to emails, resumable and scheduled on GitHub Actions, with zero paid APIs. Proof: runs on a schedule in GitHub Actions.
- [ai-wealth-advisor](https://github.com/intikhab49/ai-wealth-advisor): A RAG and tool-calling financial assistant for portfolio risk: VaR, Sharpe, drawdown and diversification scoring. Proof: LangChain · ChromaDB memory · Flask.
- [secureface](https://github.com/intikhab49/secureface-liveness-detection): Face recognition access control with head-pose liveness, rPPG pulse detection and vector matching. Proof: InsightFace · OpenCV · ChromaDB.
- [cryptoaion](https://github.com/intikhab49/cryptoaion-price-prediction): A BiLSTM-with-attention price prediction API with WebSocket streaming and JWT auth. Proof: PyTorch · FastAPI · WebSockets.

- [kubernetes-flask-crud](https://github.com/intikhab49/kubernetes-flask-crud) (archived early project): Flask + PostgreSQL CRUD app deployed on Kubernetes (Minikube) behind an NGINX reverse proxy with NetworkPolicies, plus a Docker Swarm stack.
- [kubernetes-flask-microservices](https://github.com/intikhab49/kubernetes-flask-microservices) (archived early project): Flask microservices on Kubernetes (Minikube + Flannel) and Docker Swarm: NGINX reverse proxy, PostgreSQL, logging service, Prometheus monitoring and NetworkPolicies — a hands-on DevOps project.
- [react-express-drizzle-crud](https://github.com/intikhab49/react-express-drizzle-crud) (archived early project): Full-stack TypeScript CRUD app: React + Vite, Express, Drizzle ORM, Neon Postgres, Passport session auth with scrypt hashing and a Postgres session store.
- [ubuntu-dev-tools-installer](https://github.com/intikhab49/ubuntu-dev-tools-installer) (archived early project): Interactive Bash script to install or update Python, VS Code, Docker, Jenkins and kubectl on Ubuntu — detects installed versions and asks before changing anything.

## How I work

1. Scope it in writing: A short spec with the acceptance checks agreed before any code, so “done” means the same thing to both of us.
2. Build in parallel: AI coding agents and people work behind the spec, a claims board and test gates, so speed does not cost correctness.
3. Prove the behavior: Scripted call batteries for voice agents, end-to-end suites for apps, benchmarks for models. Results go in writing.
4. Ship and hand over: Deployed, documented and monitored, with the numbers that went against us reported too.

## Stack, and where each tool was used

- AI and LLMs: Claude (rag-cost-curve, the Slack triage system, pushback), Claude Code (the multi-tenant platform build, diff-gate, pushback), MCP (fairfax, which runs as an MCP server for coding agents), Codex (the multi-tenant platform build, as part of the agent team), DeepSeek (the multi-tenant platform build, as part of the agent team), Gemini (ai-wealth-advisor), OpenRouter (ai-wealth-advisor), LangChain (ai-wealth-advisor), Hugging Face (Open Jev, the open typed decision engine)
- Voice: Vapi (voice agents for a mobility company, a dental practice receptionist, vapi-voice-agent-crm), Twilio (voice agents for a mobility company, vapi-voice-agent-crm), Stripe (payment-recovery calls with SMS payment links, vapi-voice-agent-crm), ElevenLabs (part of my voice-agent stack), Deepgram (part of my voice-agent stack), Retell AI (part of my voice-agent stack)
- Machine learning: PyTorch (Open Jev, cryptoaion), LightGBM (EdgeProof backtesting), XGBoost (the first crypto prediction API), ONNX (Open Jev), OpenCV (secureface liveness detection), scikit-learn (part of my ML stack), pandas (EdgeProof, the data pipelines), NumPy (every Python research project)
- Backend: NestJS (the multi-tenant platform, 148 endpoints), Prisma (the multi-tenant platform), PostgreSQL (the multi-tenant platform, lifeboat, pgvector-cpu-check), FastAPI (the lead engine, cryptoaion), Node.js (vapi-voice-agent-crm, blueprint-runtime), Express (vapi-voice-agent-crm), Python (fairfax, pdf-cpu-bench, rag-cost-curve and more), TypeScript (blueprint-runtime, the multi-tenant platform)
- Frontend: Next.js (the multi-tenant platform portal), React (the multi-tenant platform portal), Streamlit (the lead engine, secureface), Tailwind CSS (part of my frontend stack), Astro (part of my frontend stack), Vite (part of my frontend stack)
- Infra and automation: Docker (the multi-tenant platform, lifeboat, minio-from-source), Kubernetes (lifeboat for the Bitnami Helm charts, kubernetes-flask-microservices), GitHub Actions (fairfax, pgvector-cpu-check, diff-gate, the lead pipeline schedule), Cloudflare Workers (the payment-link and SMS pipeline, whofetched), Cloudflare Pages (the billing-services company website), Playwright (the multi-tenant platform, on every pull request), Slack + Notion (the Slack triage system), QEMU (pgvector-cpu-check, 7 CPU models)

## Services

- AI voice agents: Vapi and Twilio receptionists and outbound callers, wired into CRMs, payments and SMS.
- Multi-tenant SaaS architecture: Postgres row-level security, BFF auth, field-level encryption, event-driven jobs.
- RAG and LLM agents: Knowledge-base chatbots with tool calling and memory, judged by cost per correct answer.
- LLM evals and research: Calibration, benchmarks and backtests that report the losing numbers too.
- Agentic coding setups: Claude Code skills, MCP servers and CI gates for AI-written code.
- Automation and data pipelines: n8n, Cloudflare Workers, Slack and Notion, lead generation and enrichment.
- Developer tools and CI checks: CLIs, GitHub Actions and MCP servers for gov clouds, Make.com, Postgres images and more.
